h1:
Southern Khanom Jeen in Trang
Endless Veggies, Local Favorites
intro: For a lot of people in Trang, breakfast isn't rice soup or coffee — it's khanom jeen (fresh rice noodles) drowned in rich crab curry, then piled so high with fresh herbs and vegetables you can barely see the noodles underneath. Locals just call it "nom jeen," and the well-known shops open before dawn and sell out by noon. These are the khanom jeen spots people in Trang actually go to, picked from real reviews and from shops that are still open right now.

blocks.html: Khanom jeen in Trang differs from the central-Thai version because here the curry sauce (nam ya) is the real star. The famous shops usually keep several sauces going on the same morning — from crab curry made with crab from the seas around Hat Samran and Koh Sukorn, to a sweet, creamy coconut nam ya, all the way to a sharp fermented-fish curry (gaeng tai pla). Each comes with pak nao, the tray of fresh and pickled vegetables you help yourself to as much as you like. Some shops put out more than twenty kinds. That's the charm that keeps Trang's khanom jeen from ever getting old.

blocks.text: How many curry sauces are there, and how do you choose?

blocks.html: Knowing the sauces before you walk in makes ordering a lot easier. Most Trang shops let you ladle several over a single plate, so if you're not used to southern flavors yet, start with the coconut nam ya or the crab curry.

items.name: Crab curry (nam ya pu)
items.blurb: Trang's signature sauce, made by toasting sea-crab meat with the curry paste until fragrant. The flavor is rounded rather than fiery, and the crab comes in firm chunks. Several well-known shops in town built their reputation on crab curry specifically — this is the one first-timers should try before anything else.
items.meta: Crab-forward, not too spicy · easy for newcomers

items.name: Coconut nam ya (nam ya kati)
items.blurb: An orange sauce of curry paste stir-fried into coconut milk, leading with sweet richness and only mild heat — kids are fine with it. It's the one the whole family can share without anyone complaining, and it goes with every kind of fresh side vegetable.
items.meta: Sweet and creamy, low heat · good for all ages

items.name: Fermented-fish curry (gaeng tai pla)
items.blurb: For people who like it intense. Built on salty fermented fish innards with grilled fish added, it's deeply salty and spicy in the truly southern way. You have to eat it with plenty of side veggies to cut through it. Southerners love it, and it puts newcomers' palates to the test.
items.meta: Salty and very spicy · proper southern flavor

items.name: Shrimp-and-peanut sauce (nam ya nam phrik)
items.blurb: A sweeter, brown-toned sauce of shrimp and peanuts, eaten with raw veggies and boiled egg. It's gentler than the others — a palate-resetting plate when you've been eating a lot of spice.
items.meta: Sweet and mellow, not spicy · a palate reset

items.name: Jungle curry / green chicken curry
items.blurb: Some shops add a hot, coconut-free jungle curry (nam ya pa) and a green chicken curry ladled over the noodles as extra options — good if you want a change from the usual sauces.

blocks.title: Order smart
blocks.html: Many Trang shops let you ladle several sauces onto one plate — you don't have to pick just one. Try mixing crab curry with the coconut nam ya for the full range of flavors, and don't forget to pile on the pak nao, since the vegetable tray is unlimited refills.

blocks.text: The khanom jeen shops locals in Trang actually eat at

blocks.html: Trang's well-known khanom jeen shops are mostly clustered in the town center (Thap Thiang). Most open before dawn and sell out before noon or early afternoon, because locals eat this for breakfast. We've picked the shops that reviews praise for their curry and side veggies, with the area, price and opening hours as far as we could confirm them.

items.name: Chuen Napha Khanom Jeen Nam Ya Pu Mueang Trang
items.blurb: One of the most talked-about crab-curry shops in Trang, using crab from the seas off Hat Samran and Koh Sukorn. The crab curry is firm and fragrant, and there's dim sum, congee, Chinese doughnuts and pan-fried eggs alongside — a full local Trang breakfast. Plates start at 30 THB.
items.meta: Thap Thiang, near Ton Samo junction · open 6:00–14:00, closed Tue

items.name: Khanom Jeen Khun Pum (Kaphang Surin)
items.blurb: A long-standing Trang institution across from Kaphang Surin public pond. The draw is that you grab your noodles and ladle the curry yourself, as much as you want, from five sauces — coconut, shrimp-and-peanut, fermented fish, jungle curry and green chicken curry. There's khao yam (southern rice salad) and fried chicken too.
items.meta: Wian Kaphang Rd, across from Kaphang Surin pond · open 7:00–noon

items.name: Wiman Khanom Jeen (Na Ta Luang)
items.blurb: A shop in the Na Ta Luang area that reviews praise for its firm crab curry, with several sauces to ladle and a tray of fresh side veggies piled high. It's more comfortable to sit at than the small stalls — good if you want to linger over a long breakfast.
items.meta: Na Ta Luang area, Mueang Trang · open morning–afternoon (about 7:00–15:00)

items.name: Khanom Jeen Pa Keng
items.blurb: A tiny shop under the trees that's been open more than 25 years. Pantip reviews call it delicious and very cheap, with small bowls starting at a bargain price. It's a homey, unpretentious place that older Trang locals still drop by regularly — good if you want the original taste without any fuss.
items.meta: Under the trees, Mueang Trang area · very budget-friendly

items.name: Khanom Jeen Je Waew
items.blurb: A newer shop making waves for its variety, with seven sauces — coconut, fermented-rice chicken-foot, green chicken curry, fermented fish, crab, a rich grilled-fish curry, and a sweet fresh-shrimp sauce. The pak nao runs to more than 20 kinds, both fresh and pickled, plus steamed fish curry (haw mok) and fish cakes on the side.
items.meta: Choem Panya Rd, near Darunothai School, Thap Thiang · 7 sauces

items.name: Khanom Jeen Khun Pum (in-town branch)
items.blurb: Another well-known shop in town that reviewers praise for its sweet, creamy coconut nam ya and friendly prices. Good for a breakfast stop before heading out — but it sells out fast too, so go early.
items.meta: Trang municipal area · opens early, sells out fast

items.name: Khanom jeen stalls in Thap Thiang morning market
items.blurb: If you'd rather not hunt down a specific shop, walk into Trang's fresh market in the morning and you'll find khanom jeen stalls ladling curry alongside dim sum and other breakfast bites — cheap, and with the real market atmosphere of local Trang life.
items.meta: Morning market, Thap Thiang area · cheap breakfast

items.name: Khanom jeen shops in Huai Yot
items.blurb: If you're passing through Huai Yot before reaching Trang town, there are southern khanom jeen shops in the markets and along Phetkasem Road to stop at — boldly southern in flavor, with fresh side veggies from gardens nearby. Good for a stop along the way.
items.meta: Huai Yot district, along Phetkasem Rd · stop along the way

blocks.text: What is pak nao, and what's on the tray?

blocks.html: Pak nao is the spread of fresh and pickled vegetables southerners eat alongside khanom jeen and other bold dishes. Its job is to cut richness and saltiness and add freshness to each bite. Trang khanom jeen shops usually set out a big tray you help yourself from, unlimited, and some offer more than twenty kinds. Grab a varied handful and eat it with the curry — you'll understand why southerners can't do without it.

items: Popular fresh vegetables — bean sprouts, cucumber, yardlong beans, pennywort, stink beans (sato), djenkol beans (luk niang), young cashew shoots
Southern wild greens — manpu shoots, liang leaves, acacia (cha-om) shoots, fiddlehead fern, with their distinctive astringent, nutty flavor
Pickles / accompaniments — sour pickled veg, shredded sour mango, shallots, fresh bird's-eye chilies, to crank up the heat
Add-ons — boiled egg, fried fish, fish cakes, steamed fish curry (haw mok), which many shops sell alongside to order extra

blocks.title: Veggie-tray etiquette
blocks.html: Refills may be unlimited, but only take as much as you can finish, and use the serving tongs in the middle of the tray if the shop provides them — it's more hygienic. As for stink beans and djenkol beans, the smell is strong, so try a little at a time if you're not used to them.

blocks.text: When's the best time to go for khanom jeen in Trang?

blocks.html: Khanom jeen is a Trang breakfast. The famous shops open from six or seven in the morning and usually sell out before noon or early afternoon. If you're set on a popular shop, go in the morning, because the good sauces — crab curry especially — tend to run out first. Several shops have a weekly closing day (Chuen Napha is closed Tuesdays), so check before you leave your hotel to be safe.

items: 6:00–8:00 — the golden hour for Trang khanom jeen: the sauces are freshly made, the side veggies are at their freshest, and shops aren't packed yet
8:00–11:00 — still an easy meal, but the crab curry is starting to run low at some shops
After noon — many popular shops are closed or sold out; only the ones that stay open into the afternoon remain, so call ahead to check

faq.q: Which khanom jeen shops in Trang are the best — the ones locals actually eat at?
faq.a: The names locals bring up most are Chuen Napha for crab curry, and Khanom Jeen Khun Pum at Kaphang Surin, where you ladle the curry yourself. For cheap, traditional eats there's Khanom Jeen Pa Keng, open more than 25 years, and Je Waew, with up to seven sauces to choose from.

faq.q: Which Trang khanom jeen sauce is best for people who don't eat spicy food?
faq.a: Start with the coconut nam ya, which is sweet, creamy and only mildly spicy, or the crab curry, which is fragrant and rounded rather than fiery — both are easy for kids and anyone new to southern flavors. Save the fermented-fish curry for later, since it's the saltiest and spiciest of the lot.

faq.q: What side vegetables (pak nao) come with Trang khanom jeen?
faq.a: There are fresh vegetables like bean sprouts, cucumber, yardlong beans, pennywort, stink beans and djenkol beans; southern wild greens like manpu shoots and liang leaves; plus pickles and shredded sour mango. Some popular shops offer more than twenty kinds with unlimited refills.

faq.q: How much does khanom jeen cost in Trang?
faq.a: Most plates start at 30 THB. Homey spots like Pa Keng have small bowls from 20 THB. Add-ons like fish cakes, steamed fish curry and boiled egg are usually 20 THB each — making it a very affordable breakfast.

faq.q: What time should you go for khanom jeen in Trang?
faq.a: Khanom jeen is a Trang breakfast. The famous shops open around 6–7 a.m. and sell out before noon or early afternoon, with crab curry going first. Aim for 6:00–8:00, and check the shop's weekly closing day first — Chuen Napha, for example, is closed Tuesdays.
